name: cloud-terminal-nix
_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh

nixdroid.tracker_dir_note: THIS IS OUR CODE. The gradle project is ac_cloud-nix-on-droid/ itself, flattened at the app root like every other app here. upstream_repo/pinned_tag are provenance: they record where the tree came from, not something the build fetches. GPL provenance lives in README.md, ATTRIBUTION.md and LICENSE.
nixdroid.app_id_note: RENAMED 2026-08-30, overriding the prior 'keep upstream id' decision: com.termux.nix -> cld.termux.nix, so this fork installs ALONGSIDE the official Nix-on-Droid app instead of colliding with it (same id + different signature previously forced the upstream app to be uninstalled first). The new id is EXACTLY the same byte length (14 chars) as the old one — mandatory, not cosmetic: this is termux-app-derived and, like Termux itself, would compile the applicationId into every bootstrap ELF binary as a fixed-length string were its native bootstrap module enabled (its native bootstrap module is disabled — 'NIX-ON-DROID: Unused'). CORRECTED 2026-09-16: this note used to conclude from that disabled module that 'no bootstrap-zip patching was needed here; its Nix store instead comes from proot bind-mounts and Context.getFilesDir() at runtime, both of which follow applicationId automatically'. That is FALSE and it is a load-bearing falsehood. The bind mounts are string literals in bin/login, a script the upstream bootstrap GENERATES with /data/data/com.termux.nix/files/... written in 22 times (plus 8 in usr/lib/login-inner); nothing in this app reads getFilesDir() to build them. An unpatched bootstrap therefore execs a proot-static under a package directory that is not installed. Equal byte length is what makes the fix a pure find+replace — see bootstrap.package_name_rewrite below, which now performs it. Equal length keeps the option open without relinking anything if that module is ever re-enabled, and matches the sibling cld.termux rename in ac_cloud-termux/build.json for the same reason. See TermuxConstants.TERMUX_PACKAGE_NAME / app/build.gradle applicationId+manifestPlaceholders for the source-side rename.

build._doc: Stock termux-app gradle: assembleRelease, signed with the ONE shared constellation keystore. signing=vault_jks_env, NOT 'keystore' — that is not a mode the engine has, and an unrecognised value matches no branch and signs with the debug key instead, silently. A debug-signed build never receives the signature-level CLOUD_EXEC permission, so the bind fails the same way it does when the app is not installed at all.

signing_env._doc: Consumed by _resolve_signing in the fork engine and read back by the release signingConfig added to app/build.gradle. The tokens are the engine's vocabulary — keystore_path|store_password|key_password|key_alias — and it fails loud on anything else.

bootstrap._doc: The proot + glibc root filesystem, BAKED IN at build time instead of downloaded on first run. Until this block existed, TermuxInstaller.java popped an editable text box on first launch pre-filled with this url_base and streamed bootstrap-<arch>.zip straight into a ZipInputStream: no network meant no terminal ever, a host nobody here controls sat in the boot path, and NOTHING verified the bytes before marking them executable. The download now happens once, in CI, against the sha256 pinned below, exactly the way ac_cloud-termux/app/build.gradle::downloadBootstraps has always fetched the Termux bootstrap. Nothing enters git: *.zip is gitignored and the artefact lands in app/build/, so the committed diff is this JSON.
bootstrap._doc_why_it_is_the_runtime: This zip is not packaging convenience, it is the runtime. It carries bin/proot-static (built aarch64-unknown-linux-android, so bionic Android runs it natively) and, underneath it, glibc-2.37-45 including lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 and lib/libc.so.6. A glibc CLI has no loader on Android otherwise -- #288 proved that with ELF evidence. proot supplies the glibc root; the terminal is what makes those binaries runnable at all.
bootstrap._doc_dns_bridge: #758 where a shell in this terminal resolves names: through the app's SystemDnsBridge (libs/sysdns), i.e. Android's resolver, i.e. whatever the SuperApp's Configs > Mesh > DNS applies. The pinned zip's etc/resolv.conf -> /etc/static/resolv.conf names two public resolvers (measured), and `nix-on-droid switch` would put them back, so bake_default_packages.py does not edit that file: it ships `resolv_conf` (written from `nameservers`, loopback only, refused otherwise) and patches bin/login's proot exec to bind it over /etc/resolv.conf and pass -p, which moves the guest's 127.0.0.1:53 to the bridge's port. The port is `source`'s bridge_port, read by app/build.gradle into BuildConfig for TermuxService, never restated here. Same shape as ac_cloud-termux/rootfs/rootfs.json::dns_bridge.
bootstrap._doc_url_residual: url_base is a THIRD-PARTY host and it is still in the BUILD path, though no longer in the boot path. The sha256 pins below mean a compromised or vanished host fails the build loudly rather than shipping different bytes. Mirroring these two zips to our own GH release and repointing url_base is the follow-up; it changes this value and nothing else.

artifact._doc: #618 — the baked zip is ~400 MB, so it is not baked directly into THIS app's APK. It used to be an APK asset, which made every one-line app fix a 400 MB update that every phone re-downloaded in full just to get the code. #628 Slice 2 changed the TRANSPORT again: rather than a bare GH release asset TermuxInstaller downloads at runtime (the shape this block described through Slice 1), the bytes now ship inside the companion APK declared at release.companions[] (id rootfs-nixdroid) — a real, installed, signature-verified sibling package with no network involved at all. This block remains the content-address DECLARATION (identity_files → the 12-hex version every asset name below is built from); it no longer names a publish step, because there is nothing left to upload here — the companion machinery publishes the APK that carries these bytes, gated on its own paths_from so an app-code change never touches it.
artifact._doc_id: {id} is the first 12 hex of sha256 over identity_files — the content address of everything that DETERMINES the baked zip: this declaration (url_base, release, the per-arch sha256 pins, the nixpkgs pin and attrs) and the two scripts that transform it. A pin or script change yields a NEW asset name, so it is uploaded and every phone refetches; an app-code change yields the same name, so nothing is uploaded and no phone refetches. That is why there is no hand-maintained version to forget to bump. {abi} is the release.variants[] id.
artifact._doc_identity_files_795: #795 -- proot.json pins and fetch-proot.py fetches the bin/proot-static this zip ships in place of the 24.05 bootstrap's own.
artifact._doc_identity_files_771: #771 -- rootfs-extras.nix builds goose, hermes and the noexec shim into this zip; it reads goose's and hermes' version and url from ac_cloud-termux/rootfs/rootfs.json (so a bump there must re-address this zip too, even though it also moves on termux-only edits to that file: a stale address is the false green, an extra republish is only bytes); noexec-shebang.c is the shim's source and gitconfig ships as etc/gitconfig.
artifact._doc_identity_files_store: #644 -- the five ab_cloud-terminal-store entries are here because the link store is BAKED INTO THIS ZIP (usr/lib/cloud-store) and the login-inner patch sources it. Leave them out and an engine fix keeps the old content address: the asset is not uploaded, no phone refetches, and CI is green over a rootfs that still carries the broken engine -- the exact false-green shape #618's address was introduced to prevent. Paths are app-relative and resolved with os.path.join/new File(projectDir.parentFile, ...) by both readers (cloud-android-fleet-manifest-guard.py::_content_address and app/build.gradle::bootstrapArtifactId), so "../" reaches the repo root.

bootstrap._doc_asset_name: Name inside the APK's assets/. One per APK, not one per architecture: each release.variants[] entry builds its own APK, so baking all four would multiply the size for three rootfses that APK can never run.
bootstrap._doc_package_name_rewrite: MANDATORY, and the reason this app's app_id_note used to claim otherwise is a bug that was corrected 2026-09-16. The note said the Nix store 'comes from proot bind-mounts and Context.getFilesDir() at runtime, both of which follow applicationId automatically'. It does not: bin/login inside the zip is a GENERATED shell script whose every path is a literal, and it hardcodes /data/data/com.termux.nix/files/... 22 times, with 8 more in usr/lib/login-inner (30 occurrences across exactly 2 text entries of 4056; no ELF binary and no SYMLINKS.txt entry contains it). Unpatched, $PREFIX/bin/login execs a proot-static under a package directory that is not installed and the terminal dies ENOENT naming a path that belongs to a different app. Both ids are 14 bytes -- which is exactly why the 2026-08-30 rename was length-preserving -- so patch_bootstrap_ids.py does a pure find+replace and hard-fails if any 'from' survives or if the entry count moves.
bootstrap._doc_archs: Keyed by the Android ABI in release.variants[].abis, valued with the arch token upstream names the zip after and the pin for it. size is the unpatched download; the patched copy is slightly larger because re-deflating is not byte-identical (aarch64 37,671,948 -> 37,841,339; x86_64 39,291,055 -> 39,515,852), which is why only sha256 is enforced and size is documentation.

default_packages._doc: #595 -- agent tooling BAKED into the store this terminal ships, same 'no first-run install' rule #348 applied to the runtime itself. Without this block a fresh install has Nix and nothing else: upstream's own first login (usr/lib/login-inner) is an INTERACTIVE, NETWORKED wizard -- it prompts 'set up with flakes? (y/N)' on stdin and only then fetches/builds a config -- so 'open the terminal, run claude' would otherwise need a Y/N answer and a build before any tool exists. bakeBootstrap realizes these attrs as a real Nix profile generation on the CI runner (native: the runner's CPU already matches system, no proot/qemu needed for the BUILD, only the shipped rootfs needs proot to RUN on Android) and bake_default_packages.py copies that generation's whole closure into the same nix/store/ the id-rewrite already produced, points nix/var/nix/profiles/per-user/nix-on-droid/profile at it, drops etc/UNINTIALISED so the wizard is skipped, and patches usr/lib/login-inner's one unconditional session-init line to fall back to a baked PATH script when $HOME/.nix-profile (which the wizard would have created) does not exist.
default_packages._doc_nixpkgs_pin: nixos-unstable HEAD as of 2026-09-25, read via github:NixOS/nixpkgs/<pin>#<attr> flake refs so the CI-built closure is reproducible. All three attrs below are stdenv-built nixpkgs packages (not raw npm/apt), so their ELF interpreters are already patched to /nix/store paths -- the same mechanism every other binary already in this bootstrap relies on to run under the shipped proot with no generic /lib.
default_packages._doc_attrs_737: #737 -- zsh, gh, curl, jq, ripgrep, fd, openssh, sops, age and which are here because ab_cloud-terminal-store/store.json::toolset now declares the tool set BOTH terminals ship, and this list is how the nix terminal installs it. That supersedes the #641 audit's 'deliberately left out' for curl, openssh and ripgrep: the bar is no longer 'a shell or an agent calls it by name' but 'the terminal is a complete agent workstation on first launch', and the termux terminal already carried all of them through the fleet tool belt. python3 stays out (#665). The names on PATH are NOT listed in `binaries` below -- they come from the toolset, and render-store.py refuses a repeat; `provides` still maps each attr to them so the declaration-level gate can prove every toolset name has an attr behind it before nix runs.
default_packages._doc_login_shell_attr: #641 -- which baked attr becomes the LOGIN shell. bake_default_packages.py retargets the generated usr/lib/login-inner's `usershell="..."` assignment at profile_link + /bin/<this>, and hard-fails the build if that path is not a real, chmod-ed zip entry. MEASURED, not inferred: the pinned aarch64 zip (sha256 64afc02d..., byte-identical to the pin) generates usershell="/nix/store/q2j9ncs2b0zd7gbla21ck3jj4knpj23y-bash-5.2-p15/bin/bash" and contains no fish binary at all (only curl's and nix's fish COMPLETIONS), which is why #594 making fish the default for cloud-terminal-termux never reached this app. Upstream's own -x guard and its `exec -l bash` fallback below the assignment are left alone, so a fish that somehow did not ship still yields a shell.
default_packages._doc_attrs_audit: #641 -- audited as a whole rather than grown one defect at a time. git/nodejs_22/claude-code are #595's original agentic payload. coreutils (#640) is ls/cat/env. fish is the login shell. bashInteractive is NOT redundant with the bash inside the zip: that one is reachable only as /bin/sh and is on no PATH, while claude-code's own Bash tool spawns `bash` by name and login-inner's last-resort `exec -l bash` also resolves by name. findutils/gnugrep/gnused/gawk/less are what git subcommands and an agent's shell calls actually invoke (git's pager IS less; without it `git log` cannot page). DELIBERATELY LEFT OUT: curl and wget (the store already carries nix's own curl and nothing in the boot path needs a fetch), gnutar/gzip (only `git archive` wants them), procps, openssh, python3, ripgrep (claude-code ships its own), and the nix-on-droid/home-manager wizard machinery this whole block exists to avoid. Each addition is ~tens of MB in a payload that is already ~370 MB, so the bar is 'a shell or an agent calls it by name', not 'it would be nice to have'.
default_packages._doc_gitMinimal: #665, from #664's measurement -- this attr was `git` and is now `gitMinimal`. It is still THE canonical git (same source, same version, `bin/git`, full push over HTTPS via git-remote-http); `binaries` and `provides` still say `git`, so nothing on PATH changes and #644's build-time gate is satisfied unchanged. What moves is the closure. MEASURED on the live artifact, not estimated: the shipped rootfs is the companion APK's assets/bootstrap.zip (393,621,704 B, 21,281 entries, 387,858,100 B compressed over 202 store paths), and nixpkgs `git` drags python3-3.14.7 (73,582,754 B compressed, 19.0% of the whole rootfs) plus perl-5.42.3 and 40 perl modules (17,436,391 B, 4.5%) plus the git-2.55.0-doc output (4,967,911 B) into it. At this pin `gitMinimal = git.override { withManual = false; pythonSupport = false; perlSupport = false; ... }`, and NO_PYTHON=1 / NO_PERL=1 remove exactly seven subcommands: git-p4 (python) and git-send-email, git-instaweb, git-cvsimport, git-cvsexportcommit, git-archimport, git-cvsserver (perl). Every one of those seven was grepped for across this whole repository and appears nowhere, so the saving is 95,987,056 compressed bytes -- 24.7% of the rootfs -- for no tool anything calls. ALSO DROPPED, and the one real behaviour change: gitMinimal sets withpcre2 = false, so `git grep -P` and `git log --perl-regexp` lose PCRE. Both were grepped for repo-wide with zero hits, and pcre2-10.48 stays in the closure for gnugrep regardless, so standalone `grep -P` is unaffected. Do not 'simplify' this back to `git`: that re-adds 96 MB to a payload every phone downloads in full.
default_packages._doc_coreutils: #640 -- coreutils is here for ONE path that is not a user-facing tool: /usr/bin/env. The bootstrap zip ships usr/bin/ EMPTY (verified across all 4056 central-directory entries of the pinned aarch64 zip: no usr/bin/env entry, no */bin/env anywhere, no SYMLINKS.txt line for it), and the only thing that has ever created it is upstream's first-login wizard -- which default_packages exists precisely to skip (etc/static/UNINTIALISED is dropped). #638 stopped the terminal DYING on that absence; it could not make `#!/usr/bin/env sh`, the commonest shebang there is, work. bake_default_packages.py::env_symlink_line emits a SYMLINKS.txt line for usr/bin/env pointing at profile_link + /bin/env, i.e. at THIS attr, and hard-fails the build if that target is not a real zip entry listed in EXECUTABLES.txt. Do not remove coreutils from attrs believing it is a convenience package: the bake step will fail loudly, which is the point.

extras._doc: #771 -- profile entries no nixpkgs attr can supply, built by `expr` (a function of the pinned nixpkgs for the target system) and installed into the SAME profile as `attrs`, one `nix profile install --expr` per entry of `attrs` here. goose and hermes are the termux terminal's own (ac_cloud-termux/rootfs/rootfs.json is their one declaration: version, url, arch names); at this nixpkgs pin goose-cli is another release and hermes-agent is not packaged. `pins` is the one thing that file does not carry and a fixed-output fetch needs: the content hash, keyed by the version it was taken for, so a rootfs.json bump without a re-pin fails evaluation by name. goose's per-arch hashes are GitHub's own release-asset digests (re-measured by download); hermes' is PyPI's sha256 of the py3-none-any wheel. noexec-shebang is ab_cloud-terminal-store/noexec-shebang.c, preloaded through etc/ld-nix.so.preload from `preload` under profile_link; their names are provided[] like any attr's, and B2 counts them.

default_packages._doc_binaries: #737 -- this terminal's tools BEYOND store.json::toolset (which every consumer prepends: render-store.py::tools_of). Repeating a toolset name here is refused at render time.

wake_lock._doc: #787 Termux's 'Acquire wakelock', ON by default: TermuxService takes a partial wake lock (plus the Wi-Fi lock when wifi_lock) whenever a session is open and drops it when the last one ends (com.termux.cloud.CloudWakeLock decides; test/test-wake-lock.sh runs it). The notification action still turns it off, and that choice persists. Read by app/build.gradle into BuildConfig; the build fails if either key is missing. State: GET /api/terminal/wakelock (also /api/terminal).

companions._doc: #628 Slice 2 — the bootstrap becomes an INSTALLABLE fleet library APK (com.diegonmarcos.cloudlib.rootfsnixdroid, gradle :rootfs-lib), not a bare release asset TermuxInstaller downloads at runtime. This is the ONLY declaration that makes it so; the engine reads release.companions[] generically (#628 Slice 1) and builds/publishes/gates this entry with no code change here. Gated on its OWN content address (identity_files + module_dir, derived; #796), not the app's, so an app-code-only change (e.g. a UI fix) never rebuilds or republishes the ~400 MB payload — that blast-radius regression is exactly what #618 fixed for the bare asset and what this gate keeps fixed for the APK that now carries it. KNOWN AND ACCEPTED SIDE EFFECT: forks.nixdroid.bootstrap.artifact.identity_files still lists build.json itself, so adding this block moves that artifact's content address ONCE, on this commit — an honest move (the transport genuinely changed from a downloaded release asset to a baked APK asset) and the derived gate is what stops it from recurring on every future companion-unrelated edit.
companions._doc_module_dir_796: #796 -- the gate's inputs are DERIVED, not listed: forks.nixdroid.bootstrap.artifact.identity_files (reached through fleet-lib.json's declared_in/at pointer, the same content address the fleet row's version_name is built from) plus this wrapper module, whose gradle and manifest are bytes of the lib APK. The paths_from list this replaces gated on the whole of ab_cloud-terminal-store/, so an edit to pty-selftest.py republished ~400 MB that had not changed; the engine now refuses a paths_from outright, because a second declaration of the same inputs is one that can drift.

ghcr._doc: DISABLED, and disabled is the TRUTH rather than a preference: ship-cloud-nix-on-droid.yml has no GHCR step at all — no docker/login, no oras push — so nothing has ever created the cloud-nixdroid package. Verified 2026-09-10 by enumerating all 431 container packages under the diegonmarcos account: cloud-nixdroid is not among them, and /user/packages/container/cloud-nixdroid answers 404 to a token that reads cloud-terminal fine. This key said `true` while that was so, which is not a harmless overstatement: regen.sh emitted the image name into the fleet manifest, the updater probed it whenever the release channel hiccuped, and GHCR answers an anonymous caller 403 DENIED — not 404 — for a package that does not exist, because confirming absence would leak private package names. That 403 is what the owner saw on the phone. gh_release below is genuinely the only channel for this app, exactly as its own _doc says. To give it a registry channel, add the push step to the workflow and flip this back — in that order, so the declaration never leads the pipeline again.

gh_release._doc: Rolling 'latest' release: the ONLY channel for this app, since GHCR would publish it private. asset_name was inherited as cloud-comms-dialer.apk when this block was copied from the dialer — an install URL pointing at a different app entirely. regen.sh's fork branch derives the store asset as image + '.apk' and so was never wrong, which is exactly why the bad value could have sat here unnoticed.

variants._doc: Same shape as ac_cloud-browser and every other per-ABI app here. CLOUDNAV_VARIANT selects one; the engine exports .abis as CLOUDNAV_ABIS for gradle and names the artifact from .gh_asset, so the two matrix jobs cannot overwrite each other in one dist dir.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. This app had NO tests block at all, so every ship run asserted only that it compiled -- which is how an APK that downloads its entire runtime from a stranger's domain on first launch, with no integrity check, shipped green for months.

shell._doc_requires: Tools the testers shell out to, checked BEFORE any of them runs, so a missing tool is a loud red instead of an assertion quietly answering from its absence. test-bootstrap-baked.sh reads build.json with python3; test-noexec-shebang.sh compiles the #771 shim with cc.

tests._doc_unit: tests.unit.task is deliberately UNSET: this fork has no JVM test source set, and the engine reports that as a named coverage gap on every run. Declaring a task that runs nothing would convert an honest gap into a false green.
